chapter_theme: Forbearance (பொறையுடைமை), on the title's word: in the attached heart lies a lizard that grips the senses, and checking it is great patience. The other verses turn to the Lord's goodness, the grace that kings and jnanis reach, and the dancer's endless rhythm; their link to forbearance is not plain.
structure_note: Only 539 speaks of forbearance (கமை, kshama) in so many words; 540 to 542 concern the Lord and his worshippers and may have been grouped here by an editor.

539.reading: In the heart of those who cling there is a lizard; grown full, it lies tangled about the nose and tongue, and to keep it from flourishing in the mind it ravages is great forbearance.
539.nuance: கமை is forbearance (Sanskrit kshama). The lizard is not named: it may be desire or anger, and the nose and tongue may be the senses, or breath and speech in a yogic reading. The variant நாவியும் for நாவையும் changes tongue to musk.

540.reading: The countless gods ringed by their court, bowing at the feet of him whose body is like milk so that they might be saved, said: 'King even of Vishnu and of first Brahma, in the world this one is truly good.'
540.nuance: The variants rewrite the verse: மேனி பணிந்தடியேன் தொழ makes the poet the worshipper, and ஞாலத்து நம்மடி நல்கிடென்றாலே makes the last line a plea, 'grant us your feet in the world'. Forbearance enters only if the Lord's goodness to supplicants is meant.

541.reading: Those in whom knowledge has ripened are kings at our side, worshipped with joined hands by armies ringed round from every quarter; they can reach the grace of the First of the gods, who makes the flesh grow.
541.nuance: ஊனை விளைத்திடும் (who makes the flesh grow) may be the Lord as maker of bodies. ஏனை விளைந்தருள் (variant வளைந்தருள்) is unclear. The verse may also mean that kings with armies worship the jnanis.

542.reading: By strong ways and many ways, at home and in the hall, practising and setting the steps, the dancer who leaps from the field has a rhythm without limit.
542.nuance: கூத்தன் is Siva the dancer and மன்று his hall, but மனையிலும் மன்றிலும் may also be the body and the inner space. கொல்லை (field, cremation ground) and இலயம் (rhythm, absorption) both carry yogic readings.

links.note: The Kural asks for bearing wrongs done to one and then forgetting them; Tirumular places forbearance inward, as checking the creature of craving that grips the senses. Both call it forbearance, but the Kural's is toward others and Tirumular's toward oneself.

162 says that at death the body's dancing rhythm has ceased (ஆடும் இலையமும் அற்றது); 542 says the dancer who leaps from the field has a rhythm without limit (எல்லையிலாத இலயம்). The same word marks the body's rhythm that ends and the Lord's that does not.

source_issues: 540: variants மேனி பணிந்தடியேன் தொழ, ஒப்புநீ and ஞாலத்து நம்மடி நல்கிடென்றாலே change the speaker and the sense of the last line; line 3 ends with a full stop mid-verse.
540 to 542 do not obviously concern forbearance; the chapter grouping may be editorial.
